newsitem.title: TURKEY: Defiant Islamists fete Ottoman Istanbul conquest.
newsitem.headline: Defiant Islamists fete Ottoman Istanbul conquest.

text.p: Turkey's Islamists on Thursday came out in force to mark the 544th anniversary of the Ottoman conquest of Istanbul and protest moves by the secularist establishment and the army to undermine them.
"We are here with the excitement of the new conquests we have to make," Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan told the cheering 30,000-strong crowd gathered in Istanbul's central Inonu stadium.

"And If we want to make new conquests we really have to believe," he said. "Only the National Vision (Islamists) can do this, only the National Vision can fill stadiums like this -- others do not even dare try."

Erbakan, whose 11-month-old government with the conservatives is shaking amid speculation it may finally collapse under pressure from the powerful secularist army, said these conquests would be "spiritual and technological".

Erbakan has in the past worried secularists by claiming that the Islamists would "re-conquer" Istanbul with the building of a mosque in central Taksim square, seen as the symbol of a modern, European Turkey.
The prime minister's speech was regularly interrupted by cheers and chants of "You can't shut down Welfare" and "Imam Hatip's cannot be closed."

His government is being pushed by the army to implement a series of measures against Islamist zeal, including an education plan which would reduce the role of religious "Imam Hatip" schools, and a top prosecutor has filed a case to have his Welfare Party shut down for endangering secularism.

Istanbul's Islamist mayor Recep Tayyip Erdogan told the crowd that the taking of Byzantine Constantinople by Sultan Mehmet the Conqueror opened a new era of tolerance and understanding and swept away the backstabbing intrigues of the collapsing Byzantium.

He likened Byzantium then with Turkey now, with its agenda taken up by speculation over the dangers of Welfare, whether the fractious opposition parties can unite to overthrow the government or whether the military will have to do it for them.
He slammed Welfare's critics as "backward and ignorant", a charge often levelled against Welfare supporters.

"Let us not darken our country with the arguments we have been having over the past few months," Erdogan said. "I am sure the nation that wiped Byzantium out of the history books can preserve itself from the danger of becoming like Byzantium."
Sultan Mehmet the Conqueror marched into then Byzantine Constantinople 544 years ago on May 29 to claim the city for the Ottoman empire following a 54-day seige.

The conquest celebrations have grown since Erdogan won his seat in 1994, and become an Islamist victory showcase since Welfare came a narrow first in polls in December 1995 and finally struck a coalition deal with the conservatives in June last year.
During Thursday night's festivities, which began when Erbakan swept into the stadium in a helicopter, this seige was recreated.
A group of people dressed as Ottomans dragged a wooden ship mounted on wheels around the stadium as Mehmet's troops are said to have done to get a fleet overland into the waters of the Golden Horn.

A troupe of "Ottoman warriers" stormed a mock wall defended by Byzantines and a Sultan Mehmet, mounted on a white charger, cut down the "enemy" on the battlefield before claiming victory and parading around the stadium under a shower of fireworks.
The real conquest, which lasted nearly eight weeks, was rather less simple and much bloodier.

Writers at the time reported days of pillage by Turkish troops -- who apparently fought so determinedly after Mehmet promised they could pillage -- and blood running down the gutters towards the Golden Horn, staining the waters, and severed heads bobbing up and down by the shore like rotten melons.
